verses.text: Joseph threw himself on his father's body. He wept over him and kissed him.
Then Joseph ordered the doctors who served him to prepare his father's body for burial. So the doctors embalmed Israel.
It took a full forty days, because that is how long it takes to embalm a body. And the Egyptians mourned for him for seventy days.
When the days of mourning had passed, Joseph said to Pharaoh's court, "If you are pleased with me, please speak to Pharaoh for me. Tell him,
'My father made me promise and said, "I am about to die. Bury me in the tomb I dug for myself in the land of Canaan." Now please let me go up and bury my father. Then I will come back.'"
Pharaoh said, "Go up and bury your father, as he made you promise."
So Joseph went up to bury his father. All Pharaoh's officials went with him: the leaders of his court and all the leaders of Egypt,
as well as all the members of Joseph's household, his brothers, and those belonging to his father's household. Only their children and their flocks and herds were left in Goshen.
Chariots and horsemen also went up with him. It was a very large group.
When they reached the threshing floor of Atad, near the Jordan, they cried loudly and bitterly. There Joseph held a time of mourning for his father for seven days.

When the Canaanites who lived there saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, "The Egyptians are holding a time of deep mourning." That is why the place near the Jordan is called Abel Mizraim, which means "mourning of the Egyptians".
So Jacob's sons did for him what he had commanded them.
They carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre. Abraham had bought it, together with the field, from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place.
After burying his father, Joseph went back to Egypt, together with his brothers and all the others who had gone with him to bury his father.
When Joseph's brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, "What if Joseph holds a grudge against us and pays us back for all the wrongs we did to him?"
So they sent a message to Joseph, saying, "Before your father died, he left these instructions:

'This is what you must say to Joseph: Please forgive your brothers for the wrong they did and for the sins they committed in treating you so badly.' So now, please forgive the sins of the servants of the God of your father." When their message came to him, Joseph wept.
Then his brothers came and threw themselves down in front of him. "We are your slaves," they said.
But Joseph said to them, "Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?
You planned to harm me, but God planned it for good. He did it to save many lives, as is happening now.
So then, do not be afraid. I will provide for you and your children." And he comforted them and spoke kindly to them.
Joseph stayed in Egypt, along with all his father's family. He lived a hundred and ten years.
He lived to see the third generation of Ephraim's children. The children of Makir son of Manasseh were also placed on Joseph's knees when they were born.
Then Joseph said to his brothers, "I am about to die. But God will surely come to help you and take you up out of this land to the land he promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob."
And Joseph made the Israelites make a solemn promise. He said, "God will surely come to help you, and then you must carry my bones up from this place."
So Joseph died at the age of a hundred and ten. They embalmed his body and put it in a coffin in Egypt.
